issues.failure_explanation: The finite-set estimate and the theorem's own proof require a multiplicative factor exponential in d, namely C^d. The stated sample bounds omit it, while the stated constants are only allowed to depend on the entry distribution. Thus the displayed hypotheses do not imply the condition actually used in the proof when d varies.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the required C^d factor into both sample-size bounds, or provide a new moment/concentration argument whose constants are genuinely independent of d.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed polynomial-in-d measurement complexity for uniform trimmed geometry preservation, and its informal summary, are unsupported.
issues.title: Trimmed TensorRIP sample bound drops the exponential dependence on tensor order
issues.why_classification: The source-supported repair introduces exponential dependence on tensor order, materially worsening a central advertised measurement rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now, note that (e.g., \cite[Lemma 2]{zhang2018median}), $\|\vu_{(k)} - \vv_{(k)}\| \leq \|\vu-\vv\|_\infty$ for any two vectors $\vu$ and $\vv$ and their $k$-th order statistics.

Without loss of generality, we can also assume that the rows $\{\va^\vx_i\}$ and $\{\va^{\hat{\vx}}_i\}$ of $\mat{A}^{\vx}$ and $\mat{A}^{\hat\vx}$ respectively have been reordered such that,
    $$ |\mat{a}^{\vx}_1{\vx}| \leq |\mat{a}^{\vx}_2{\vx}| \le \dots \le |\mat{a}^{\vx}_{m-k}{\vx}| \text{ and } |\mat{a}^{\hat{\vx}}_1{\hat{\vx}}| \leq 
    |\mat{a}^{\hat\vx}_2{\vx}|_2 \le \dots \le |\mat{a}^{\hat\vx}_{m-k}{\hat\vx}| .$$

issues.failure_explanation: The trimming order is determined by absolute values, but the vectors being subtracted retain their signs and generally use different row permutations. Lipschitz control of scalar order statistics does not imply the displayed bound for the signed, permuted measurement vectors. For example, signed lists (1,-1.1) and (1.1,-1) are coordinatewise close before sorting, but sorting by magnitude pairs 1 with -1 and -1.1 with 1.1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the signed-vector comparison by a valid stability estimate for the norm or sum of the retained squared order statistics, and redo the ensuing error calculation.
issues.overall_effect: The extension from a finite net to all low-rank tensors is not proved, so the uniform conclusion of the trimmed TensorRIP theorem remains unsupported independently of its sample-size issue.
issues.title: Net-extension proof incorrectly matches signed measurements after sorting by magnitude
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial replacement argument could preserve the same theorem and rates; the existing inference itself cannot simply be used.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The desired result follows by the union bound argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The quoted trimmed-mean theorem gives failure probability alpha for one fixed vector when k=ln(8/alpha). Applying it to p vectors and taking a union bound gives failure probability at most p alpha, not alpha. To obtain total failure alpha by this argument, the per-vector parameter must be alpha/p, which changes the trimming level to ln(8p/alpha). The proof also switches the quoted theorem's sample-count condition to the wrong symbol before later using m.

failure_location.quote:
we consider their embedding with respect to the data-driven row trimming of $\mat{A}^{\vx_i}_k$ with $\vx_i = \algoname{Vec}(\tX_i)$ and $k = \ln(8/\alpha)$, 
 and $\alpha \geq 4e^{-cp}$. If $m \geq C^d \delta^{-2}\ln(4p/\alpha)$, then
$$\left|\left\|\mat{A}_{k}^{\vx_i} \vx_i\right\|_2^2 - \left\|\vx_i\right\|_2^2\right| \leq \delta  \left\|\vx_i\right\|_2^2\text{ for all } i \in [p]$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: The direct source-supported repair is to use per-point failure alpha/p and trim k=ln(8p/alpha) rows, then propagate that much larger trimming level through the uniform theorem. Preserving k=ln(8/alpha) would require a new uniform concentration argument.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-set guarantee is false as derived, and the main uniform theorem cannot use it to claim high probability while removing only logarithmically many rows independent of the net cardinality.
issues.title: Finite-set trimming lemma cannot obtain a union bound with the stated trimming level
issues.why_classification: The direct repair makes the number of removed rows depend on the exponentially large covering net, withdrawing the central promise that only about ln(n) rows suffice; no source-supported argument preserves that promise.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes only a one-step recurrence involving the time-t factor and ||R^t||. Iterating such a recurrence yields a product of the factors from the preceding iterations, not the single time-t factor raised to t+1. No assumption makes the factors constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the stated bound by the proved one-step recurrence, or state the product over iteration-dependent factors and verify the indexing.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed pathwise convergence bound from the initial residual is unsupported; only the one-step estimate proved at the end remains available.
issues.title: TrimTIHT theorem states an iterated bound not established by its proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem can retain a comparable pathwise result after a limited weakening to a recurrence or product, without new global proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Let D=1+mu_t||A_t||_2 sqrt(Delta_t) and a=|1-mu_t Delta_t|. At the stated upper bound xi_t=16a^2/(17D^2), the squared approximation contribution is D^2(2xi_t+xi_t^2), whose first term alone is 32a^2/17>a^2. Hence the approximation term cannot be replaced by a as claimed. The displayed minimum is also undefined because no indexing set is supplied.
